extracted.intended_audience: aspiring short-story writers / creative writers learning craft
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for composing short stories that are tightly focused in character, plot, style, and ending, suitable for writers learning or refining their short fiction craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Critical Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit cast to essentials; merge or cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the character list small so each character advances the story. Combine minor roles or remove extraneous figures to preserve clarity and emotional focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center Around One Pivotal Event
rubrics_metrics.description: One pivotal moment, not multiple plotlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the story around a single decisive event or turning point. Avoid multiple plotlines—short stories should concentrate on a singular plot or main event within a compressed timeframe, distinguishing them from novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open with a Strong Hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Action, tone-setting, questions, or thematic statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with something that immediately grabs the reader: an action, a clear tone, an intriguing question, or a thematic line. The opening should establish stakes, voice, or curiosity quickly in the limited space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore Different Writing Styles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with form and voice to find the most effective mode for the story—e.g., epistolary/journal formats, interior monologue, poetic language, or stories told almost entirely through dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: End on a Powerful Note
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude once message conveyed; leave memorable moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finish the story as soon as the theme or effect has been achieved. Aim for an ending that lingers—a vivid image, a striking final line, or an emotional revelation—rather than unnecessary resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length & Scope Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: 1,000–10,000 words; 'a singular plot or one main event' within compressed timeframe — distinct from novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target a word count between about 1,000 and 10,000 words and keep narrative scope tight. The story should feel compressed and focused on a single plotline or event rather than multiple arcs.
